Replay

Room admission and private coordinator storage

5 min readOdin × GodotPage source ↓
On this page ↓
API and ownershipInvite and retry rulesClient handoffStorage and compatibilityVerification

replay/provision supplies the server-side create/invite/join state machine for an authority-controlled room. Room owns an existing authority.Service; its durable Bundle contains the authority record, member credentials, enrollment retry records and invite consumption. Every change uses the same revision CAS. This closes the previous gap between durable membership and separately configured service keys. The game simulation and host-migration protocol are unchanged.

The SQLite store also provides durable room checkpoint publication with separate revision CAS, typed validation and atomic metadata/bytes. The authenticated transfer endpoints have native TLS restart acceptance. The standalone service now registers the three compiled game models; Room/Party owns publication and authenticated cold restore with native/browser acceptance. Game models/dependencies must still opt into the typed service contract; see published restore.

The create/join protocol and Godot connection now expose this backend through a bounded room hub and verified TLS. Native create/join/restart acceptance passes on loopback. The client journal adds durable native/browser enrollment. Shared Party menus and Room recovery are integrated into multiple example games. Public deployment, human accounts, global room discovery and room retirement remain separate product/deployment work. Tests use isolated provisioning and profile data; these local gates are not public reachability claims.

API and ownership#

Odin
import provision "godot:replay/provision"
import storage "godot:replay/provision/sqlite"

// Server setup: private path, stable room ID and deployment-selected content/policy.
// Keep these owners at stable addresses; call provision.close before storage.close.
store: storage.Store
room: provision.Room

// For creation only, the creator has generated and retained a fresh Secret.
// Check errors at every boundary. An existing room must be loaded, not recreated.
bundle, make_error := provision.make_room(room_id, content_id, creator_claim, endpoint)
open_error := provision.open(&room, bundle, storage.commit, &store, authority_clock, control_wire)

// Only return credentials after successful durable creation/admission.
creator, creator_error := provision.creator_grant(&room, creator_claim)
ticket, invite_error := provision.invite(&room, creator_claim, invite_secret, .Player)
guest, join_error := provision.join(&room, ticket, guest_claim, guest_endpoint)

// Existing authority RPC and rendezvous code use this same live service.
authority.service_pump(&room.service)

The abbreviated example assumes storage.open has succeeded and that room lookup has established absence. On restart, call storage.load and pass its complete bundle to provision.open; do not rebuild a bundle from gameplay archives. The authority service advances its persisted coordinator generation and applies the existing lease quarantine. A second owner fences the first owner's subsequent CAS writes. Calls on one owner are serialized, including packet delivery.

Room IDs and allowed content/policies are the hosting application's responsibility. A create client must retain the same requested room ID and creator claim across retries. The hub atomically resolves competing creates and returns existing grants only after verifying the creator claim and original endpoint/content. Corrupt records are never interpreted as absent rooms. The backend does not allocate global room IDs or keep an unbounded map of rooms.

provision.secret() obtains 32 cryptographic random bytes on supported native targets. An explicit Entropy callback supports other runtimes and deterministic tests; it must provide cryptographic entropy in deployment. Unsupported runtime entropy, zero values and generated credential collisions fail. No pseudo-random fallback is provided. Generate the creator claim, invite secret and each enrollment claim independently, before submitting their corresponding request.

Invite and retry rules#

  • .Player grants membership and its control/gameplay credentials. It grants no authority-backup or hosting permission. This role does not choose a gameplay seat or restrict the game's own spectator admission policy.
  • .Trusted_Peer explicitly grants co-op hosting and permission to receive complete authority backups. It is refused for dedicated rooms; infrastructure enrollment needs trusted deployment administration.
  • The creator claim authorizes invite issue/revocation. Creator administration is separate from the current gameplay host and does not move on host migration. Disabling the creator member also disables its invite administration.
  • An invite has a fixed role and finite use limit. Repeating its issuance with the same secret and parameters returns the same ticket. Changed parameters or a revoked ticket are refused. Exhaustion never refills the invite.
  • Join retries must present the same ticket, enrollment claim and original endpoint. A committed retry returns the same control key and stable game token, plus the member's current incarnation. It consumes no further use and performs no write. Changed payloads and disabled members are refused.
  • Revoking a ticket prevents new enrollment. It does not ban previously enrolled members or prevent them from recovering a lost successful response. Trusted membership administration still uses authority.coordinator_member through room.service.coordinator; its commit is routed into the same private bundle.
  • Process Challenge/Rebind can update an enrolled member's incarnation/endpoint. The original enrollment endpoint remains stored solely to identify exact join retries. Ordinary RPCs still require the current bound nonce/incarnation.

Membership, control key, game token, retry record and invite decrement enter one durable transaction. An error publishes no grant and no in-memory partial join. A storage failure poisons the running authority: the backend does not guess whether the commit reached storage. Reloading in a fresh owner resolves that uncertainty.

Capacity is currently 16 lifetime member slots and 16 lifetime invite slots per room, with at most 15 uses per invite. Disabled members and revoked/spent invites remain tombstones. IDs, credentials and old retry proofs are never recycled into new members. Long-lived public rooms will need an explicit bounded retirement and credential lifecycle before these limits can be expanded safely.

Client handoff#

An authenticated, confidential provisioning frontend returns only the caller's Grant. Populate the Godot Room_Options.identity, .key, .room, and .session.token from that grant; require .session.network.content to match its content. The creator is the room's bootstrap member (stable member ID 1). Keep provisioned_incarnation=false so a newly opened game process goes through the existing challenged registration flow. The grant is a membership credential, not a live authority lease. Do not use its host permission as a substitute for the coordinator's current grant.

Control/gameplay endpoints and ENet/WebSocket/RTC connection settings remain deployment inputs. Client credentials need private durable storage before users can rely on fresh-process reconnect. Enrollment secrets must not appear in URLs, logs or public rosters. Providing the backend over a plain public socket does not provide the confidentiality that credential issuance requires.

Storage and compatibility#

replay/provision/sqlite is native macOS/Linux storage. It reuses the authority store's checked WAL/FULL/fullfsync connection settings and writes a distinct replay_provision table. Compare/read/write happens within BEGIN IMMEDIATE. New files are exclusively created with mode 0600. Existing files with group/other permissions, symlinks and non-regular files are refused without changing them. The caller must supply a private directory and protect SQLite sidecars/backups; the bundle is plaintext at rest. Missing-file creation is explicit. Existing corrupt records are retained and produce a read error, even when creation is enabled.

The bundle format is version 1, canonical kind 0x5052, with its authority revision in the envelope tick and game content ID in the content field. It contains decision record version 3. The gameplay protocol (7), checkpoint (4) and authority RPC (2) are unchanged. Older authority-only database rows cannot be upgraded without a trusted source for their missing keys and game tokens; no automatic import or fallback is attempted.

The private bundle is never a migration checkpoint. A trusted gameplay successor may receive full simulation state but does not receive room administration claims, control keys, unused invite capabilities or other members' game tokens.

Verification#

Shell
nix develop --command bash tests/replay_provision/run.sh
nix develop --command bash tests/replay_provision_sqlite/run.sh

Core tests exercise exact retries, revoked/exhausted invites, disabled/rebound members, dedicated policy, entropy failure, capacity, uncertain commits and a complete authenticated authority handoff using newly enrolled credentials. The package also checks for freestanding WASM; this does not claim browser provisioning. SQLite tests cover reopen, another owner's CAS, read-only storage, corrupt blobs and private file modes. Separate process-kill fixtures interrupt a real join before and after SQLite commit and verify the corresponding retry behavior in fresh processes. See recorded evidence.
